strategic_horizon.terminal_goal: Build a personal weak-network VPN for OpenWrt/Linux to Linux or Windows with TCP-shaped FakeTCP outer packets, UDP/datagram-like no-HOL inner behavior, DTLS 1.3, and a small efficient FEC implementation suitable for owned endpoints.
strategic_horizon.current_milestone: Fast steady-state sizing at a normal 200 Mbit/s public-link budget, with 20:20 fixed and TUN excluded.
strategic_horizon.local_optimization_stop_rule: Prefer high-information measurements over broad grids. Treat 200 Mbit/s as public-link capacity: with 20:20, drive about 90 Mbit/s inner payload so FEC plus DTLS/FakeTCP headers approach the 200 Mbit/s outer budget. Only repeat points that show a cliff or anomaly.

continuation_cursor.last_completed_action: The user asked to skip broad low-rate testing and go directly to a normal 200-Mbit/s RTT/loss resource test, then decide whether UDPspeeder can be removed in favor of a small WBD-owned FEC layer. A local fixed-rate C UDP probe was developed and directly validated at 200 Mbit/s on loopback with 100% delivery, but the current sandbox cannot provide reliable tc netem because sch_netem is unavailable in its user namespace and repeated unshare/netns experiments wedged the sandbox executor. Therefore the impairment run was moved to the already-qualified privileged Ubuntu runner instead of treating a userspace relay as netem. Repository commits 162235f78ecc3e2a923eb981623399366b439247, a4a225b1595f20bc19dbd1a33c8d85d667a8b875 and 916804dc31096040d7b264d2c69a3bf5f6993251 added scripts/udp_rate_probe.c, scripts/bench_v2_transport_200m.py and .github/workflows/transport-200m.yml. The focused workflow runs RTT 20/100/300/600 ms in parallel; each job sweeps symmetric per-direction loss 0/1/5/10/20%, shapes each public direction to 200 Mbit/s, sends 90 Mbit/s inner 1200-byte datagrams for 2 seconds, and records delivery, p50/p95/p99/max, outer gross rate/drop counts, per-component CPU, endpoint CPU-core fractions and peak RSS. PR #3 is temporarily titled [200m]; this sequence-31 commit is the synchronize event intended to trigger the new workflow.
continuation_cursor.current_task: Complete the 20-case focused 200-Mbit/s public-link sweep, inspect CPU/RSS and delivery/latency cliffs, then use those results plus the known UDPspeeder RSS dominance to decide the FEC replacement design.
continuation_cursor.why_now: The user wants efficient resource sizing rather than the previous 126-case characterization. 20:20 roughly doubles coded traffic, so shaping the public link to 200 Mbit/s while offering 90 Mbit/s inner payload models a realistic 200-Mbit/s WAN more honestly than offering 200 Mbit/s inner and then blaming the 2x FEC overhead for oversubscription.
continuation_cursor.done_when: transport-200m completes four RTT jobs and aggregates exactly 20 rows; each row has delivery, latency percentiles, gross outer rate/drop counts, client/server CPU-core fractions and RSS. The temporary [200m] PR title is removed. The result is summarized in handoff, and the next FEC step is explicitly chosen: keep UDPspeeder temporarily or replace it with a fixed systematic 20+20 erasure codec with bounded buffers and timer flush.

udp_like_status.current_200m_definition: 200 Mbit/s public capacity per direction; 90 Mbit/s inner offered load to leave room for approximately 2x FEC plus DTLS/FakeTCP headers
udp_like_status.focused_200m_surface: RTT 20/100/300/600 ms x symmetric loss 0/1/5/10/20% = 20 steady-state cases, one fast pass; repeat only anomalous/cliff points

udp_like_status.kernel_netfilter_probe: run 32816368578 PASS at 300Mbps UDP: route/filter/NAT all ~299.9Mbps and 0% loss; no throughput cliff from small-rule-set netfilter/NAT
udp_like_status.fec_replacement_candidate: A small WBD-owned systematic Reed-Solomon-style fixed 20+20 erasure layer is technically feasible and is the leading simplification candidate; simple XOR parity alone is not equivalent because it cannot recover arbitrary multi-packet erasures in a 20:20 budget.
